notes: CTRY-GB: sourced pack data, not legal advice or a live integration. Source access dates use UTC (2026-11-01). Maintainer acceptance occurs through PR review.

Pack-wide verification is secondary: the four nation codes are confirmed by government guidance, but the 217 child subdivisions and their parents are a Unicode CLDR 48 snapshot, not independently checked against the current ISO register. It includes legacy administrative areas such as Cumbria; do not use it as a current local-authority or permitting-authority list. Engine kind region/district is a neutral schema mapping, not an asserted ISO category.

English uses engine locale en and country-derived Intl tag en-GB. Welsh (cy) is a welcome contributor language, not an installed engine locale. English names are the fallback in other interface languages; no new translation review is claimed.

The postcode expression is a permissive shape check, not Royal Mail deliverability validation. Phone nationalLength 10 is representative, not a complete numbering rule (short and exceptional numbers exist). Europe/London is the representative zone; dependencies and overseas territories are not included in GB.

UTR is sensitive tax information and is deliberately absent from registrationIdentifier and the identifiers facet. The v2 identifier contract has no sensitivity or projection field; do not add it as a public identifier before that contract and its authorization tests exist.
No EU layer is inherited. Northern Ireland-specific trade and VAT arrangements are not inferred from EU membership or this pack; specialist review remains necessary.

Holiday data is bounded to the GOV.UK published 2026-2028 dates, including substitute days and the 2026 Scotland World Cup bank holiday. No dates are extrapolated; local Scottish public holidays and individual employment/site calendars are not included. Bank holidays do not automatically grant paid leave.

Every named adapter is a candidate only. No lookup, filing, identity verification, payment, tax calculation or document signing is performed. Standards are linked, not copied or licensed for indexing.
